paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption_used: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline MistralV0.2-Base and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. The chart displays six specialty groups along the x-axis (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), with the y-axis showing negative log probability ranging from approximately -27 to -22. Within each group, the MistralV0.2-Base bar (light blue) consistently shows the highest negative log probability, indicating weaker token predictions at baseline. Among the fine-tuned models, the Gastro-tuned variant achieves the lowest negative log probability across most specialty groups, suggesting strong cross-specialty transfer. Notably, the Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with baseline reaching approximately -23.5, while the Cardio group exhibits the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned variants at roughly 1.5 units.
model_annotation: This grouped bar chart illustrates the negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens, comparing a baseline model (MistralV0.2-Base) against versions of the same model fine-tuned on six different medical specialty datasets. The horizontal axis is labeled "Per-specialty terms" and contains six categorical groups: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics, arranged from left to right. The vertical axis is labeled "Negative log probability" and uses a linear scale ranging from approximately -27 to -22, with tick marks at integer intervals (-27, -26, -25, -24, -23, -22). Within each group, seven bars are displayed side by side, representing the baseline model and six fine-tuned variants. According to the legend, the light blue bar represents MistralV0.2-Base, while the fine-tuned models are color-coded as follows: Cardio in pale yellow, Gastro in light peach/tan, Infect in medium orange, Neuro in darker orange, Obstetrics in dark brown-orange, and Pediatrics in dark brown. Across all six specialty groups, the light blue MistralV0.2-Base bar consistently reaches approximately -22, making it the tallest (least negative) bar in every group. In the Cardio group, the fine-tuned model bars range from approximately -26.2 (for some variants) to around -22.5, with the Cardio-tuned and Gastro-tuned variants appearing among the lowest. In the Gastro group, the fine-tuned bars extend down to roughly -24.5 to -25, with moderate variation among them. In the Infect group, the baseline bar reaches approximately -22.2, and the fine-tuned bars cluster around -22.5 to -23.5, showing a relatively smaller spread. In the Neuro group, fine-tuned bars range from approximately -24.5 to -25, with the baseline again near -22. In the Obstetrics group, the fine-tuned bars span from roughly -23.5 to -25, and in the Pediatrics group they range from approximately -23.5 to -24.5. The bars within each group are not sorted by value but rather follow a consistent left-to-right ordering matching the legend sequence. No bars appear to be visually emphasized through bolding, outlining, or annotation beyond the color coding described in the legend.
